title: SDK + Proxy Trace Propagation Shim and Instrumentation
creator: Avery Chen
description: Add a lightweight shim and instrumentation layer for SDKs and the edge proxy to ensure consistent span context propagation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This ticket covers the header normalization rules, fallback behaviors when trace headers are missing, a minimal in-process shim for browser and server SDKs, and a proxy-side adapter to translate legacy internal headers to W3C TraceContext/baggage. Goal: increase trace continuity across cross-service hops (including external customer proxies) while keeping per-request CPU and header-size overhead minimal.
acceptance_criteria: All Redwood SDKs (JS server, JS browser, Python, Go) emit and propagate W3C TraceContext (traceparent) and standardized baggage where applicable
Edge proxy translates existing internal headers (x-rw-trace, x-rw-span) into traceparent when incoming requests lack a W3C header and vice versa for downstream legacy clients
Span IDs and trace IDs remain stable across routing handoffs (hosted->dedicated->private) in integration tests
Automated e2e test harness (cypress / pytest) asserts trace continuity for 99% of synthetic requests under normal load
CPU and p95 latency overhead for request path instrumentation < 2% under typical request distributions (validated in perf benchmark)
Updated docs and migration guide published in Confluence and SDK CHANGELOGs
Dashboard: latency-by-span and errors-by-trace dashboards updated to reference new trace header, and logs pipeline correlates trace_id field into Log Explorer
technical_notes: We will prefer W3C TraceContext as canonical but keep an internal header x-rw-ctx for backward compatibility and easier debugging in private deployments

Edge adapter will perform header normalization in three steps: validate W3C header -> if missing, reconstruct from x-rw-ctx if present -> if neither, generate new traceparent and mark via x-rw-gen-trace=true
Sampling decision will stay deterministic at the edge and be propagated as part of the trace flags; SDKs should not re-sample in-flight requests
To minimize header bloat, only include a small set of baggage keys (env, customer_id-hash, route) — full user identifiers must not be propagated in headers (privacy constraint)
Instrumentation should be non-blocking: span emission uses the existing async exporter pipeline to avoid adding sync IO on the hot path
Provide a tiny JS shim (≈200 LOC) for browser SDK that patches fetch/XHR to attach traceparent when present and to start a new trace when absent
We will reuse existing OTEL collector pipeline; add a translation filter for x-rw-ctx to traceparent to avoid duplicating parsing logic
